grammatical_subclaims.claim: yakka has hypothetical and factual concessive readings.
ponte has an ordinary make-small meaning.
grammatical_subclaims.confidence: high for lexical meaning; computing-specific use not established
grammatical_subclaims.evidence_status: supported by indexed primary dictionary passage

grammatical_subclaims.claim: VP + ka somo ki is a negative construction; here it follows the pixel predicate, rather than qualifying the earlier size predicate.
grammatical_subclaims.confidence: high for construction; application of the analysis is model linguistic interpretation

grammatical_subclaims.claim: The Latin and Kana originals contain the same targeted a=ponte / アポンテ, yakka / ヤッカ and ka somo ki / カ ソモ キ construction.

analytical_gloss.text: Even if/although one makes the file smaller, the pixels are not changed.
analytical_gloss.label: Analytical working gloss of the middle sentence only; not an accepted full translation.
analytical_gloss.limits: The glossary terms, complete string, naturalness and computational terminology were not independently accepted. This is not native-speaker attestation.

reasoning_summary: The size-reduction clause precedes yakka; the following clause supplies the pixel-preservation assertion. The hypothetical reading does not guarantee reduction; the factual concessive reading may assume it. The cited descriptions do not select one reading for this UI. A bare make-small verb or absence of an explicit possibility auxiliary is insufficient to prove the F01 categorical-size defect. Conversely, yakka alone does not prove an unequivocal may-reduce qualification.
